project: Migrate the 33 Global-Stub/Spy UI Tests to Bun and Reprofile
description: Migrate the 33 frozen global-stub/spy-only UI test files from Vitest compatibility execution to the existing native Bun sublane, preserve all 176 source-level named cases and 183 executable cases exactly, eliminate Vitest fallback for those files, and report matched before/after lane wall times without changing product behavior or test taxonomy.

context.customerAsk: Migrate the 33 global-stub/spy-only Vitest files listed by the UI latency handoff through the existing ui/src/testing/bun compatibility seam, preserve every describe/it contract and exact cohort case count, and report matched before/after lane wall times in the PR.
context.problem: The UI unit lanes still pay roughly 35 seconds of Vitest compatibility-process overhead for 33 tests whose global stub, spy, and restore requirements are already supported by the shared Bun seam, slowing correctness feedback and retaining unnecessary dual-runner ownership.
context.solution: Move the eight frozen cohorts incrementally to exclusive Bun execution beside their existing owners, prove exact behavioral and executable-count parity after every cohort, confirm zero Vitest selection, then run lane and frontend gates and publish reproducible focused and aggregate before/after timing evidence.

acceptanceCriteria: All eight frozen cohorts run under Bun with exact executable totals: API 01 5 files / 17 cases, API 02 3 / 20, dashboard components 01 4 / 11, current-factory-definition 01 7 / 46, current-factory-definition 02 5 / 41, current-selection 04 1 / 5, current-selection 06 4 / 9, and current-selection 08 4 / 34.

The migration preserves all 176 source-level named cases and 183 executable cases after parameter expansion without deleting, weakening, duplicating, or replacing behavioral assertions merely to satisfy Bun.
Every migrated test executes exactly once in the Bun sublane and zero times in Vitest; no renamed original, compatibility fallback, or duplicate runner membership remains for the 33 files.

Production UI behavior, public contracts, generated API artifacts, coverage membership, and browser-test ownership remain unchanged; unavoidable semantic edits are isolated, justified, and directly tested.

Matched before/after wall times and the aggregate affected lane delta are recorded in the PR with commands, host/runtime context, pass counts, and scoped conclusions, and the existing UI lane check script and CI frontend jobs pass.

Typecheck, focused cohort tests, standard UI unit/component gates, and relevant frontend verification pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved, shared or move-only files are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged.
